01: What is the purpose of an RStudio project?
Keep related scripts, data, and settings together
A project helps organize and reproduce work; it does not create an experimental design.
Which command makes an installed package available in this R session?
Installation and loading are different operations.
It records operations that can be repeated on corrected data
It guarantees every scientific assumption is true
It removes the need to inspect data
A script records the computational procedure, while scientific validity still needs review.
02: What is the result of length(c(2, 5, 8))?
length() counts elements rather than adding their values.
Which expression selects all elements of x greater than 5?
The logical condition identifies which elements to retain.
Why write a function for repeated calculations?
To name and reuse a defined operation
To make results independent of the input
A function makes a reusable computational step explicit.
03: What should a relative file path be relative to?
A documented project or working directory
Whatever folder the previous user happened to open
The largest file on the computer
Portable projects use an explicit, consistent directory structure.
To check the structure and variable types
To prove that all measurements are correct
An imported number can be misread as text; structure checks reveal this.
To record variable meanings, units, and coding
To ensure all columns are numeric
Names alone rarely capture units, missing codes, or the meaning of categories.
04: A logical indicator of missing values
is.na() identifies missingness without altering observations.
When is removing a duplicate row scientifically justified?
When it is a confirmed duplicate record, not a genuine replicate
Whenever two yields happen to be equal
Equal observations can be independent replicates; duplication concerns the identity of records.
What should a cleaning log record?
What changed, why, and how it was checked
A cleaning log makes decisions auditable and repeatable.
05: Which operation changes the number of rows by selecting observations?
Filtering retains rows that satisfy stated conditions.
What is a key risk when joining field and soil tables?
A non-unique key can multiply rows
Every join automatically sorts out units
A join proves that samples are independent
Check key uniqueness and expected row counts before and after joining.
What does grouping change when calculating a mean?
The sets of observations summarized separately
A grouped mean is computed separately for each defined group.
06: Which plot is useful for examining a continuous variable's distribution?
A pie chart of row numbers
A histogram displays counts over numeric intervals; the bin choice affects its appearance.
To make the measurement scale interpretable
To increase the number of replicates
Units connect a visual pattern to the agricultural measurement.
What does a box plot's median line show?
The middle value of the ordered observations
The median summarizes central position and is distinct from uncertainty about a mean.
07: Which summary is generally more sensitive to an extreme yield?
A sufficiently extreme observation can shift the mean substantially.
What is the unit of a variance computed from yields in tonnes per hectare?
Variance squares deviations; standard deviation returns to the original measurement scale.
Why report sample size alongside a summary?
To show how many observations support it
To remove the need for uncertainty
The same mean can be based on very different amounts of information.
08: What should happen before interpreting a suspicious trend?
Check data quality, grouping, units, and design
Delete every point outside the fitted line
Exploration includes checking how the observations were produced and recorded.
Why inspect patterns within treatment groups?
An overall pattern can conceal differences between groups
A group label proves a randomized design
Aggregated and within-group patterns can differ.
What makes an exploratory question useful?
It is connected to an agricultural problem and can guide further checks
It ignores the origin of the data
EDA develops questions and checks; it does not guarantee a preferred conclusion.
09: In a logistic growth curve, what does the asymptote represent?
The limiting level approached by the model
The measurement at every time point
A guarantee of biological maximum under all conditions
It is a fitted model parameter whose biological interpretation needs the study context.
Why inspect residuals after fitting a growth curve?
To look for patterns the model has missed
To force the asymptote to zero
To turn repeated observations into independent samples
Residual patterns can reveal lack of fit or inappropriate error assumptions.
Why should a growth model cover the observed time range?
Extrapolation beyond observed growth phases can be unreliable
Any curve predicts all future conditions exactly
Time order is irrelevant to growth
Limited observations can leave growth parameters weakly identified.
10: What does a moving average help reveal?
A smoothed pattern across neighbouring time points
A new set of independent field replicates
The exact next rainfall with certainty
Smoothing reduces short-term variation while changing the series representation.
A recurring pattern at a regular period
Monthly data can show an annual seasonal cycle, but that pattern must be checked.
To guarantee all future observations lie at the point forecast
Point forecasts alone conceal important uncertainty.
11: A specific statistical statement assessed under a test model
A conclusion that the data must confirm
A guarantee that treatments are identical in every respect
Its meaning depends on the particular test and assumptions.
Why distinguish statistical and practical significance?
A detectable difference may be too small to matter agriculturally
Every small p-value implies a profitable treatment
Effect sizes are unnecessary when p is small
Decision-making needs effect size, uncertainty, costs, and study design.
What is the role of a confidence interval?
To express uncertainty about a parameter under the method's assumptions
To show the range of every individual observation
To prove that confounding is absent
A confidence interval concerns a parameter; a prediction interval concerns a new observation.
12: Which unit determines replication in an experiment?
The unit independently assigned a treatment
Every row created by copying a spreadsheet
Subsamples and repeated measurements are not automatically independent treatment replicates.
To assess model assumptions and unexplained structure
To guarantee all treatment means differ
To choose the smallest p-value after viewing all models
Model diagnostics support interpretation rather than guarantee a desired result.
Why account for multiple pairwise comparisons?
To address increased false-positive risk across comparisons
Multiplicity matters when making a family of inferential statements.
13: What does a residual represent in regression?
The intercept plus the sample size
Residuals describe deviations from the fitted conditional mean.
Why assess regression on data not used for fitting?
To estimate how well predictions generalize
To guarantee there is no confounding
To increase the training R-squared automatically
Training fit can be optimistic; evaluation should respect the data structure.
What is a risk of extrapolation?
The fitted relationship may not hold beyond the observed predictor range
The model automatically collects more data
The prediction interval must always narrow
Predictions outside the supported range need additional scientific justification.
14: What belongs in a reproducible analysis document?
Data sources, code, explanation, and interpretation
Only a screenshot of a p-value
Readers should be able to trace how the analysis produces its results.
Why set a seed in a simulation example?
To make the pseudorandom sequence repeatable
To prove simulated data are observed field data
A seed helps reproduce a computation; it does not change the scientific status of simulated observations.
How should AI assistance be used in an R practical?
Check suggestions against executed results, documentation, and assumptions
Treat every generated function name as valid
Let the AI invent missing observations
The student remains responsible for correctness and interpretation.
